model.title: Model
model.attentionOn: Flash attention and sparse attention (QSA), always on
model.attentionInfo: Sparse attention and Flash Attention are always on for this architecture; turning either off runs out of memory above 64K context. Weights are used as quantised in the file.
model.serverOther: {{model}} is loaded now; switching unloads it first

generation.title: Generation
generation.thinkingInfo: This model's template accepts low, medium and xhigh only, and folds “high” into xhigh — so there is no fifth level to offer. A single request can override this with chat_template_kwargs.

thinkingHelp.off: The model answers directly, with no reasoning step.
thinkingHelp.low: Brief, focused reasoning that moves straight to the conclusion.
thinkingHelp.medium: The model's own default: it reasons, with no instruction steering how much.
thinkingHelp.high: Works through the task carefully, checks assumptions and weighs alternatives. Slowest.

context.title: Context and memory
context.lengthHelp: How much conversation the model can hold, reserved when it loads
context.kvTypeHelp: q8_0 halves the memory the cache takes
context.kvTypeInfo: How the attention keys and values are stored. q8_0 takes half the memory of f16: at 262144 tokens this model's K/V cache is 3.2 GB instead of 6, and the disk cache stores about 60% as much per token. Its output differs from f16's about as much as a different batch size does. The sparse-attention index stays f16 either way. Applies on the next load; the disk cache keeps only conversations saved with the type in use and removes the others.
context.promptCacheDiskHelp: A conversation that comes back is read from disk instead of processed again
context.promptCacheDiskInfo: Off by default. When on, a conversation's attention rows are written to disk once each, as they are computed, and its recurrent state - the part that changes - only when the conversation leaves memory: another conversation needs its room, or the model is unloaded (about 0.3 GB each time). When it returns it is read back instead of processed again: a 173K-token conversation in about 1.6 seconds instead of three minutes of prefill. Survives restarts; conversations saved by older versions are removed. Applies on the next load.
context.promptCacheDiskMibHelp: Beyond this the oldest conversation is removed; a long one takes several GB

concurrency.title: Concurrency
concurrency.parallelHelp: Conversations the server answers at once
concurrency.parallelInfo: Conversations kept at once: each stays in its slot, so going back to it continues where it was instead of processing it again, and several can answer at the same time. Agent tools need one for each session they run at once: with fewer, sessions push each other out and are processed again. The slots share one context pool (a single conversation can still use all of it); each beyond the first costs about 0.4 GB of GPU memory, and a conversation in use keeps up to about 0.9 GB of snapshots in RAM.
concurrency.kvPoolHelp: Tokens the conversations share; 0 means the context length
concurrency.kvPoolSingle: Takes effect with two or more concurrent conversations; one conversation’s pool is its context
concurrency.kvPoolInfo: The context memory the concurrent conversations share, when it should hold more than one of them at full length; each conversation is still limited to the context length. 0 = the context. Every token of the pool costs GPU memory: for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next about 33 KB with an f16 KV cache and 21 KB with q8_0, plus about 5 KB for the MTP draft’s mask up to 512K (beyond it the draft works in smaller steps and that part stops growing). The K/V part also counts against Windows commit (RAM + page file). Measured on a 96 GB carve with q8_0, 4 conversations and MTP: 768K fits (about 91.5 GB in use); larger pools put part of it in shared GPU memory, which works but is slower. Applies on the next load.

speculative.title: Speculative decoding
speculative.mtpHelp: Drafts tokens ahead with the model's MTP head and checks them, for faster answers
speculative.mtpInfo: Every drafted token is checked by the model before it is used; only the speed changes.
speculative.noDraft: No MTP draft found beside the model, so MTP is off. Put Unsloth's mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-shared-Q4_K_M.gguf in the model's folder and rescan: decode is about 60% faster with it.
speculative.draftHelp: Add the draft head from the releases page (mtp-…-head-iq4_xs.gguf) to the model folder for faster drafting
speculative.draftMaxHelp: Tokens drafted per step; 3 is fastest here
